bug_semantics: NodejsFunction local bundling flattened esbuild argv into one command string and passed that string to a shell. A caller-controlled externalModules value (and later define, loader, inject, or esbuildArgs values) could therefore contribute shell metacharacters that bash -c or cmd /c interpreted as host commands during cdk synth, deploy, or diff.
flaw_origin: PR #11289's atomic member 6a16cf26e7278caf27634e4b1798c8d3058461fd replaced the prior Parcel configuration path with esbuild local bundling, mapped externalModules directly to --external:${external}, joined the argv with spaces, and executed the result through bash -c. Its direct parent still used Parcel and had no externals-to-esbuild-command interpolation; the member was later squash-carried to main as 7a82850d8bec45f18791e269e988c5261d5238d4.
ai_marker: absent: the exact BIC commit object names Jonathan Goldwasser <jonathan@goldwasserexchange.be> as both author and committer and its message is only 'feat(lambda-nodejs): esbuild bundling', with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker.
evidence: CVE.org API record CVE-2026-11417 is PUBLISHED with AWS as assigner and describes command injection through externalModules, define, loader, inject, or esbuildArgs; it sets the Unix remediation boundary at 2.245.0 and Windows at 2.246.0. The AWS security bulletin 2026-041-AWS reports the same product, mechanism, CVE, and patched versions.

GitHub's first-party PR #11289 commits endpoint decomposes squash carrier 7a82850d8bec45f18791e269e988c5261d5238d4 and identifies 6a16cf26e7278caf27634e4b1798c8d3058461fd ('feat(lambda-nodejs): esbuild bundling') as the first member; the member object and parent are present in the validated full-history clone.

git show 6a16cf26e7278caf27634e4b1798c8d3058461fd -- packages/@aws-cdk/aws-lambda-nodejs/lib/bundlers.ts shows createBundlingCommand adding options.externals.map(external => `--external:${external}`), joining the esbuild command with spaces, and LocalBundler.tryBundle calling exec('bash', ['-c', localCommand]).

Direct parent-tree check at f3c8b5034eb7ad1ccd9eecb4a929c8f11a2336d0 shows the same path still implements Parcel bundling and contains no externals, externalModules, or esbuildCommand interpolation; thus the advisory's first exploitable externalModules path is absent in the immediate parent.
The exact 6a16cf26e7278caf27634e4b1798c8d3058461fd commit object has author and committer Jonathan Goldwasser, one parent f3c8b5034eb7ad1ccd9eecb4a929c8f11a2336d0, and no trailers or AI/bot marker.

Direct fix 9bf4263ea631cae7c0cfff8872ec4fb3a3164cc1 (PR #37292) replaces the local shell command with structured spawn steps and argv arrays; follow-up a92105c64c4ff30bd85f506ef4f7dec39a923871 (PR #37412) safely routes Windows .cmd shims through PowerShell with per-argument escaping.

Resolved tag commits are v2.244.0=10267a2b60806c694fa4024ec461434df33d0387, v2.245.0=776e79dc2e9b2c300d46c099c07d25764f745b57, and v2.246.0=96da2a9be0a37c1be3574d2e4a4c5a139be235b5. merge-base checks show the squash carrier in all three, 9bf4263ea631cae7c0cfff8872ec4fb3a3164cc1 absent from v2.244.0 but present from v2.245.0, and a92105c64c4ff30bd85f506ef4f7dec39a923871 absent from v2.245.0 but present in v2.246.0.
reasoning: The vulnerability is real and officially published: unescaped caller-controlled bundling values reached a host shell in the local NodejsFunction bundling pipeline. Decomposition is necessary because main contains PR #11289 as a squash; its first atomic member 6a16cf26e7278caf27634e4b1798c8d3058461fd is the smallest available commit that introduces an exploitable property-to-shell path, while its immediate parent lacks that path. Later members and commits add Windows support and more affected properties, but do not predate the Linux/macOS externalModules mechanism. Mainline carrier and tag ancestry place the flaw before v2.0.0 through v2.244.0, the direct argv-spawn fix in v2.245.0, and the Windows-safe follow-up in v2.246.0. Because the BIC commit object itself has only a human author/committer and no AI marker, later AI-related repository activity or fix authorship cannot attribute the BIC; the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
